data.name: Khasaanah
data.gender_notes: Khasaanah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Given by Allah, magnificent, noble, beautiful, graceful, generous. The name Khasaanah carries the meaning “Graceful, beautiful” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khasaanah usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, beautiful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifies the blessings and grace bestowed by Allah
data.etymology: Khasaanah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, beautiful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khasaanah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: خساءه
in_arabic.meaning: خساءه تعني الخسارة أو الفقدان في بعض المعاني العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم خساءه يعود إلى الجذر العربي 'خ س ا' والذي يحمل معاني الخسارة أو الفقدان. ويرتبط هذا الاسم بفكرة التعويض أو المكافأة على الخسارة، وقد ورد في بعض التفاسير القرآنية ذات الصلة بالتعويض الإلهي.

in_urdu.name: خساعہ
in_urdu.meaning: خساعہ کا مطلب ہوتا ہے نقصان یا خسارة، خاص طور پر ایسا نقصان جو کسی کے لئے عظیم الشان ہو
in_urdu.long_meaning: خساعہ نام عربی جڑ 'خ س ا' سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے نقصان یا فاقد ہونا۔ اردو میں، اس نام کو اکثر ایسے شخص کے لئے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جو کسی نہ کسی شکل میں نقصان یا فاقد رہا ہو، لیکن پھر بھی ان کی قدرتی یا روحانی معاوضات کو تسلیم کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: खसाना
in_hindi.meaning: खसाना नाम का अर्थ है नुकसान या हानि, विशेष रूप से महत्वपूर्ण नुकसान
in_hindi.long_meaning: खसाना नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल 'خ س ا' से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है नुकसान या अभाव। हिंदी में, इस नाम का उपयोग अक्सर ऐसे व्यक्ति के लिए किया जाता है जिसने किसी न किसी रूप में महत्वपूर्ण नुकसान या अभाव का सामना किया है, लेकिन उनकी प्राकृतिक या आध्यात्मिक मुआवजे को भी स्वीकार किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: خسانه
in_pashto.meaning: خسانه دى دتاوان يا زيان معنا، په ځانګړي ډول يو ډول زيان چي د پام وړ وي
in_pashto.long_meaning: خسانه نوم د عربي ريښو 'خ س ا' څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چي د زيان يا تاوان معنا ورکوي. په پښتو کې، دا نوم اکثر د داسې کسي لپاره کارول کيږي چي کوم ډول تاوان يا زيان يې منلی وي، خو د هغوی طبيعي يا روحاني بدلون منل کيږي.

in_english.name: Khasaanah
in_english.meaning: Khasaanah means loss or damage, particularly significant or substantial loss
in_english.long_meaning: The name Khasaanah originates from the Arabic root 'خ س ا' (kha-sa-a), which conveys meanings of loss, damage, or deprivation. In Islamic tradition, this name may symbolize a person who has experienced significant loss but is also acknowledged for their resilience or spiritual compensation. The term relates to themes of divine recompense and personal fortitude in the face of adversity.

pronunciation.pashto: په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل خسانه (kha-sā-nah)

data.cultural_impact: The name Khasaanah holds a significant cultural value in the Islamic world. The name, derived from the Arabic word "khass" which means "exclusive, select or chosen," has been immortalized in various forms of Islamic art, literature, and history. In the Arabic culture of yesterday and today, the name Khasaanah has often been bestowed upon children who were born after much hardship or difficulty, suggesting their exclusive nature, or upon those who hold a noble position in society, making them esteemed figures.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, Khasaanah's meaning is deeply rooted in Islamic values and beliefs. The name's association with being given by Allah speaks to the Muslim belief in predestination and divine will. The added connotations of magnificence, nobility, beauty, gracefulness, and generosity connect the bearer to various aspects of the divine as well as the Prophetic character of Muhammad (pbuh). Arabic names with spiritual significance are deeply held in the Islamic community, as they inspire reflection, piety, and a connection to the rich heritage of Islamic culture.
